evidence_used: Object appears to be a cardboard box with flat opposing sidewalls suitable for parallel jaw contact.
Cardboard surface has slight porosity and micro-texture which reduces optimal gecko dry adhesion compared to smooth glass or polished plastic.
Visual scale suggests a moderate object weight.
calculation_summary: F_normal = F_base_weight_counteraction + F_adhesion_penalty_factor = 2.0 N + 1.5 N = 3.5 N
assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or friction coefficient was provided, leading to visual estimation uncertainty.
Cardboard porosity impairs the maximum dry adhesion capability of the gecko pads, requiring increased normal force to maintain a secure grasp.
Object payload weight is estimated visually from standard box dimensions.
reasoning_trace: The gecko gripper relies heavily on smooth, nonporous surfaces for maximum van der Waals adhesion via its mushroom-tipped pads. The visible cardboard surface is slightly textured and porous, which degrades dry adhesion performance. Consequently, the gripper cannot rely solely on dry adhesion and must apply a higher normal force to compensate for reduced adhesive capability and depend partially on standard frictional support to lift the box securely.
